sections.title: Why Study Physiotherapy in French?
sections.lead: France attracts students interested in physiotherapy, rehabilitation, sports recovery and patient care. In France Physiotherapy education is known locally as kinésithérapie and prepares students for professional healthcare work by combining scientific knowledge, practical skills and supervised Clinical placements.

groups.text: Key advantages to study physiotherapy in France:

items: Hands-on learning: Practical classes and clinical placements give students the opportunity to develop their assessment, movement, rehabilitation and therapeutic skills.
Professional qualification: The French State Diploma in Physiotherapy is the normal entry qualification into the profession in France.
Clinical experience: Trainees may undertake placements in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, clinics and other healthcare settings.
Specialisation opportunities: Qualified professionals are able to specialise in sports rehab, neurological rehab, respiratory physio, paediatrics and others.
International experience: Studying in France offers a chance to experience \\European healthcare practices\\ and a multicultural academic environment.
Career flexibility: Physiotherapists can work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, private practices, sports settings and community health care.
\\Edu Hawk world-wide study abroad guidance\\ assists students in exploring these opportunities and understanding the requirements of studying abroad.

sections.title: Physiotherapy Courses in France
sections.lead: Physiotherapy courses in France are about the evaluation, treatment and rehabilitation of people with movement limitations, injuries, pain and some neurological or respiratory diseases.

items: State Diploma in Physiotherapy: This is the professional qualification for the standard route into physiotherapy practice in France.
University pathway at Bachelor level: Students must complete an eligible first year of university study before entry to an authorised physiotherapy training institute.

Master in Rehabilitation or Movement Sciences: Relevant Master programmes may focus on research, biomechanics, exercise science or rehabilitation. They do not automatically qualify graduates to practice as physiotherapists.
Sports Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation- Other courses may include sports injuries, exercise rehabilitation and performance related recovery.
Neurological and Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation: Further education may focus on rehabilitation following neurological conditions, surgical procedures, injuries, or chronic movement disorders.
Research in Physiotherapy - Graduates can look into research programs in movement science, biomechanics, public health or rehabilitation.
Duration of course
The normal duration of studies is \\five years from the French baccalauréat or equivalent school-leaving qualification\\ : one eligible year at university and four years of physiotherapy training.
The 1st year is selective and not all university programs give you access to all physiotherapy institutes.

sections.title: Eligibility to study physiotherapy in France ?
sections.lead: \\Physiotherapy France eligibility\\ is based on your previous educational background, nationality and the chosen admission route.

items: \\Secondary education\\ equivalent to the French baccalaureate.
Adequate academic background, especially in \\biology and other sciences\\
Completion of an eligible first year university pathway.
Meet the \\selection criteria\\ of the respective physiotherapy institute.
Good \\French knowledge\\ for attending lectures, practical training and for communication with patients.
Other documentation required for clinical placements and University registration

sections.title: Eligibility for Indian Students
sections.lead: Indian students who have completed Class 12 should not think that they can get into a French physiotherapy institute on the basis of their school certificate alone. The normal route is an eligible first year of university study. Please check the exact route with the university and associated IFMK.

items: Students who already have a \\physiotherapy degree\\ may have a different route to apply. Admission and partial exemptions are not automatic, even if French rules provide for particular selection procedures for some applicants with non-EU qualifications.

sections.title: Physiotherapy Admission Requirements in France
sections.lead: The \\admission procedure in France for physiotherapy\\ is dependent on the institution and the applicant's category.

items: Prospective students should be prepared to submit the following:
\\Academic transcripts and secondary school certificates\\;
University transcripts (if applicable)
A \\valid passport\\ or other accepted ID.
Proof of \\French-language skills\\, if required.
a \\motivation letter\\ or other application documents, if necessary.
Certified translations of academic documents if needed.
Details of any prior healthcare education or employment, if applying via a special pathway.
Other health and vaccination records before clinical placements where applicable.

A good knowledge of \\French\\ is particularly important in physiotherapy, as students need to understand the instructions given in a clinical setting, discuss treatment strategies, and communicate with patients. Accepted language certificates and minimum levels required vary by institution.

sections.title: Physiotherapy Cost of Study in France
sections.lead: The \\total cost of studying physiotherapy in France\\ depends on the institute, public or private, the student's fee category and the city of residence.

items: Training fees and tuition

There is no national \\tuition fee\\ for all physiotherapy institutes. Training fees can differ significantly between institutions and eligible students may be able to apply for regional funding or other financial support.

Tuition fees For example, IFMK Saint-Michel has published \\tuition fees of €9,200 for the 2025-2026 academic year\. This is just one example from one institute and shouldn't be taken as a current price for all schools or a confirmed fee for 2026-2027.
Living expenses
Students should plan for:
\\Housing and utilities.
Food and daily expenses.
\\Public transport.
Insurance requirements and health related expenses.
Books, study materials and practical tools.
\\Visa and administrative expenses\\, if any.

Cost of living varies by location. Paris is often much more expensive than other cities in France, so it's a good idea to compare accommodation options and transport costs before deciding which institute to choose.
Depending on eligibility, students may be able to explore \\regional grants\\, school-based aid, or funding with healthcare employers.

sections.title: Admission Procedure for physiotherapy in France
sections.lead: The \\application process for physiotherapy in France\\ varies according to your academic background and the admission procedure of the institute.

items: 1. \\Search physiotherapy schools:\\ Look for accredited courses, location, tuition fees, clinical experience opportunities, and language requirements.

2. \\Find the right university path:\\ Typical choices include eligible university courses in \\health sciences\\, \\biology\\, \\STAPS (sports and movement sciences)\\ or other specified science and health courses.

items.title: Check international eligibility: Contact the university and IFMK to ask if your foreign qualifications are accepted for the intended pathway.
items.desc: 4. \\Prepare your application documents:\\ Collect transcripts, identity documents, French-language evidence and any additional supporting documents.

items: 5. \\How to apply:\\ The procedure will depend on your situation and will be done through specific procedure established by the institution.
6. \\Full selection requirements:\\ Entry to physiotherapy training is competitive and depends on the number of places available and the selection criteria.
7. \\Accept the offer and enrol:\\ Follow the enrolment instructions and complete any health or placement formalities required by the institute.
8. \\Apply for your student visa:\\ Complete the official \\French student visa process\\ if necessary.
For \\international students\\The exact process should be checked before applying, as the usual home route may not be the same as the route for those with overseas qualifications.

sections.title: Accreditation and Recognition of Physiotherapy in France
sections.lead: The \\French State Diploma in Physiotherapy\\ (\Diplôme d'État de masseur-kinésithérapeute\) is the standard \\professional qualification for working as a physiotherapist in France\. Students should ensure the institute they choose is accredited to provide training for this qualification.

items: You don't automatically become a physiotherapist just because you have a related degree in \\sports science\\, \\rehabilitation research\\ or \\movement science\.
Indian students recognized

Students who are intending to return to India should check the current \\professional recognition and registration requirements\\ with the relevant Indian authorities before applying. They should also verify that the precise French qualification and route of training meet the criteria applicable to the role they have in mind.

sections.title: Physiotherapy in France : Salary & Employment Opportunities
sections.lead: Qualified physiotherapists in France can work in a variety of healthcare and rehabilitation environments, provided they have the \\necessary professional registration\\ and \\work-authorisation\.

items: You could get into:
Physiotherapist at a hospital.
\\Rehabilitation centre physiotherapist.\\
\\Physiotherapist in private practice.
\\Sports rehabilitation therapist.
\\Musculoskeletal rehabilitation professional\\
\\Neurological rehabilitation therapist.
\\Respiratory rehabilitation therapist.
Practitioner of rehabilitation for the elderly or children.
\\Teaching or research positions\\ where additional qualifications are relevant.
What to Expect in Salary

\\Physiotherapy salaries in France\\ vary depending on the type of establishment in which the physiotherapist works, for example a hospital, rehabilitation centre or private practice. Experience, working hours, location, patient volume and employment arrangements also affect earnings.

faqs.q: How many years does it take to study physiotherapy in France?
faqs.a: In France, the standard \\physiotherapy pathway\\ requires \\five years\\ of study after the French baccalauréat or an equivalent school-leaving qualification: one year of university access followed by four years of physiotherapy training.

faqs.q: Can Indian students study physiotherapy in France?
faqs.a: Indian students may qualify, but admission will depend on their previous qualifications, their proficiency in the French language and the pathway being recognised by the university and associated institute. Before applying, they must confirm they are eligible.

faqs.q: Do I have to speak French to study physiotherapy in France?
faqs.a: \\French is generally a requirement\\ for professional training as a physiotherapist, because teaching, practical work and contact with patients are usually done in French. Applicants must check the language requirements of the institute they chose.

faqs.q: What are the study fees for physiotherapy in France?
faqs.a: Fees vary according to institute and student category. For reference, IFMK Saint-Michel published \\€9,200 for 2025–2026\\, but applicants are advised to check the current fee schedule for their institution and year of choice.
